document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {

## Overview
The Pacific Manta Research Group (PMRG) studies **oceanic mantas of the Eastern Pacific**, with a focus on the **Revillagigedo Archipelago** and collaborations in the **Gulf of California** and **Bahía de Banderas**. The program blends **citizen-science photo submissions** with researcher-led tagging and field work to track individuals, demography, movement, and injury/scar histories.[^about]

I contribute on the **communication and tooling** side—helping design the **public website** and **photo-ID submission pathway** so divers can send usable ventral-ID images with consistent metadata (date, site, photographer).[^submit]

## Quick Facts
- **Role:** Web/UX & photo-ID support (PMRG)  
- **When:** 2024 – present  
- **Skills:** content design, contributor guides, photo-ID catalog support, metadata standards, outreach

## Background and Questions
- How can we **scale high-quality, diver-submitted images** into an ID catalog with reliable **individual re-sighting**?  
- Which **regions and seasons** yield most re-sightings around Revillagigedo, and what can **injury/scar** records tell us about threats?

## Methods
- **Photo-ID pipeline:** contributor instructions that prioritize **ventral markings**, pelvic fins (sexing), and high-contrast exposure; support for **small-batch forms** and **bulk transfers** with folder/filename conventions.[^submit]  
- **Data hygiene:** enforce **date/time/location** metadata; avoid on-image timestamps; retain EXIF when possible.[^submit]  
- **Outreach materials:** boat-friendly Photo-ID guidance, FAQ, and visual examples to reduce unusable submissions.[^about]

## Results (preview)
- Increased intake of **ID-quality ventral images** and cleaner **metadata** across recent trips.  
- Building re-sighting threads and injury notes for individuals as catalog grows (summaries forthcoming).

## How to Contribute
- **Submit your photos:** follow the folder/filename pattern and send via the form or transfer service.[^submit]  
- Ideal shots: **clear ventral side**, include **pelvic fins**; use **flash/close-range** for black morphs; video can help stitch turning sequences.[^submit]
